overall: The AG found a quorum of the Halifax Planning Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating via email on Dec. 20, 2019, ordered future compliance and public release of those emails, and found no violation for the non-deliberative parts of the email.

allegations.summary: A quorum of the six-member board allegedly deliberated by email when a member emailed the entire board on Dec. 20, 2019 and the chair replied to all.
allegations.key_passage: We agree and find that both Ms. Troup’s e-mail and Mr. Andrews’s response violated the Open Meeting Law where the communications involved a quorum of the Board and discussed matters that were pending before the Board and within its jurisdiction or involved the operation of the Board which is public business within the body’s jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: A member's email requesting a copy of a letter distributed in the meeting packet was alleged to be improper deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: We do not find that portion of Ms. Troup’s e-mail in which she requested a copy of a letter to be improper deliberation.

allegations.summary: A member's email stating that withholding a letter was against the Open Meeting Law was alleged to be deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: we will not find a violation of the Open Meeting Law where a public body member attempts to warn another public body member against violating the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.

Publicly release the December 20, 2019 e-mails within 60 days of receipt of the determination, if not already done, by reading them at a meeting and listing them in the minutes, or by referencing them at a meeting and posting them with the minutes on the municipal website.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law. In addition, we order the Board to publicly release the December 20, 2019, e-mails within 60 days of receipt of this determination, if it has not already done so.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
